NDT training in Billings: how it works for Billings employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training for Billings and eastern Montana employers and technicians, live online or onsite at your refinery, shop or plant, under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis training centre in Billings. Your employer's written practice governs certification, and a Level III gives the exams. The courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for refining, pipeline, power and processing work across the Yellowstone Valley.

Billings is the industrial centre of a very large region. Three refineries operate in and around the city: Phillips 66 in Billings, Par Montana in Lockwood and the CHS refinery in Laurel. Product and crude pipelines, sugar processing, power generation, rail and heavy-equipment shops fill out the rest. The main challenge for local employers is distance. Travelling to a distant classroom takes a technician off the job for days, and outside providers charge for the same distance in reverse. That is why online theory and onsite practical work suit Billings well.

The detail below expands on the summary above. It covers which methods fit which local scopes, how SNT-TC-1A certification works, how to train a crew during a refinery turnaround year, and how Montana's radiation rules differ from most US states. Request a Billings training quote.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Billings

All courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Level I covers set-up and examination to instructions. Level II covers calibration, interpretation, evaluation and reporting. Level III preparation covers the Basic and method exams and running a programme. Recommended hours are in our training-requirements matrix.

With a smaller local labour pool, Billings employers value technicians who hold several methods. A technician with UT, MT, PT and VT at Level II can cover most of a turnaround scope. Adding PAUT or ET makes them the person the crew leans on. Senior technicians who end up running the programme can prepare through ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Billings, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. This sets the training, experience, exam and recertification rules for each method and level.
  2. Formal training. Classroom hours, online or onsite. See the requirements matrix.
  3. Experience. Supervised, logged hours on real work. Refinery integrity programmes, pipeline digs and shop fabrication all count when properly documented.
  4. General exam. Written test on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. Written test on your employer's procedures, equipment and the codes in use, such as ASME Section V, ASME B31.3 or API 1104.
  6. Practical exam. Examine real flawed specimens to procedure while a Level III observes.
  7. Vision test. Every year.
  8. Certification. Signed by the employer and valid for that employer only.
  9. Recertification. At the written-practice interval.

Many smaller Montana employers don't have an in-house Level III to give exams. That is one of the most common reasons they call us. Our SNT-TC-1A guide explains how an outside Level III fits into your programme.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Billings crews

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory that technicians can attend from Billings, Laurel, Lockwood or a remote job site without driving anywhere. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor comes to your plant or shop and teaches with your own instruments, reference blocks and procedures, then gives practical exams with Level III oversight. One trip can cover a whole crew.
  • Blended. Online theory through the winter, then a compact onsite practical block before the construction and turnaround season.

Montana's weather shapes the calendar. Outdoor pipeline and construction work slows in deep winter, and refinery turnarounds are planned well ahead. We fit training into your quiet windows and time practical exams so certifications are signed before the busy season. Ask about onsite training for your Billings crew. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Billings

Refining. Phillips 66's Billings refinery, first built in 1943, supplies fuels by pipeline, rail and truck to Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, Utah, Colorado and Washington. The CHS refinery in Laurel and the Par Montana refinery in Lockwood (formerly ExxonMobil) complete the cluster. In-service inspection uses API inspection codes, with ASME Section V for NDT technique and ASME B31.3 for process piping. Heavy crude from Canada brings corrosion and high-temperature damage mechanisms that keep UT, PAUT and ET busy.

Pipelines. Crude and product pipelines leave the Billings refineries and cross the Yellowstone and other rivers. The 2011 pipeline rupture under the Yellowstone River near Laurel is a well-known local reminder of why river crossings and integrity management get attention. Pipeline welding is inspected to API 1104, and covered tasks require operator qualification, which is separate from NDT certification.

Power and processing. Power plants in the region, including the coal-fired Colstrip station in eastern Montana, run boiler-tube and high-energy piping inspection. Sugar-beet processing in Billings and agricultural processors across the Yellowstone Valley operate boilers, pressure vessels and storage that need regular examination.

Rail, equipment and fabrication. Billings is a rail and freight junction. Repair shops for rail equipment, mining machinery and agricultural equipment use MT, PT and UT on welds and heavy components. Structural and tank fabricators weld to AWS D1.1 and API tank standards.

Radiography licensing in Montana. Unlike Texas, Louisiana or Maine, Montana is not an NRC Agreement State. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, through its Region IV office in Arlington, Texas, licenses the radioactive sources used in industrial gamma radiography in Montana. The state regulates X-ray equipment and certain other materials. Under the NRC's industrial radiography rules (10 CFR Part 34), radiographers must meet the licensee's training requirements and hold certification from an NRC-recognised certifying entity, and trainees must work under a qualified radiographer. Companies coming from Agreement States need NRC authorisation to work at temporary job sites in Montana. ASNT RT method certification covers technique and interpretation. It does not satisfy these radiation-safety requirements.

What local employers ask for. Billings employers usually want Level II in several methods, reliable records and people who can work alone on remote jobs. Some roles also require API inspector or AWS welding-inspector credentials, which candidates earn separately. Atlantis trains the ASNT method side.

Level III services and written practices for Billings NDT companies

Small NDT and fabrication companies in eastern Montana often run with one or two certified technicians and no Level III on staff. It works until a refinery client, pipeline operator or quality auditor asks to see the written practice and exam records. Atlantis provides:

  • Written-practice development to SNT-TC-1A, sized for small teams.
  • Outside Level III services, including remote and onsite exam administration, procedure and technique-sheet review, and records audits.
  • Corporate training programmes to build a multi-method crew without sending people out of state.

Book a Level III consultation to find out what your programme needs.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator covers 12 methods in five environments, including an oil and gas site and a storage tank. That is useful for technicians in Billings who can't easily get to a flaw-specimen library. Trainees can rehearse calibration, scanning and evaluation from home. The simulator is for practice only. The practical exam still uses real specimens and real equipment, in front of a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who writes the course content and provides the Level III oversight for exams.

Cold-weather NDT and remote work: what Billings technicians need to know

Eastern Montana brings two practical challenges that most Gulf Coast training programmes ignore: cold and distance. Both affect how inspections are done and how technicians should be trained, and both come up in Billings-area specific exams and practical work.

Temperature effects on ultrasonic testing. Sound velocity in steel and in wedge materials changes with temperature. A UT calibration done in a warm truck can drift when the probe and wedge go onto a cold pipe outside. Couplant can thicken or freeze. Contact conditions change on frosted or iced surfaces. Technicians need to calibrate at or near the temperature of the part, choose couplants rated for the conditions, and check calibration more often as conditions change. The same rules apply in reverse to hot process equipment inside a refinery, where high-temperature couplants and wedges and short contact times are needed. Our Billings training covers both ends of the range.

Surface methods in the cold. Penetrant materials have temperature limits for use. Below the qualified range, dwell times and sensitivity are no longer those assumed in the procedure, so the procedure has to be qualified for low temperature or the part has to be warmed. Wet magnetic particle baths behave differently in the cold as well. Technicians should know where their procedure's limits are and stop when conditions fall outside them rather than improvise.

Radiography in winter. Cold affects film handling, battery life on digital systems and crawler equipment, and the comfort and attention of crews working exclusion zones. Careful planning and radiation-safety discipline matter more when crews are tired and cold.

Working alone and far away. Pipeline, power and processing jobs across eastern Montana often mean one or two technicians hours away from their Level III. That makes procedure knowledge, good records and knowing when to escalate more important than in a large refinery crew. Technicians should be able to finish a job, document it fully and send the data for review without someone looking over their shoulder. Remote Level III support can cover review and questions, but it only works when field records are complete.

Planning the season. Many Billings employers do theory training in winter, when outdoor work slows, and hold practical exams in early spring before construction, pipeline and turnaround work picks up. Ask about a winter training plan for your Billings crew.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Billings

How do I get NDT certified in Billings?

Complete formal training, log supervised experience, pass the general, specific and practical exams under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Montana?

Yes, for theory. This helps Montana technicians who would otherwise travel long distances. The practical exam must be done hands-on, and we can arrange it onsite at your employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice's classroom and experience requirements. SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums are in our requirements matrix. Experience usually sets the pace.

Do I need a license for radiography in Montana?

Radiography with radioactive sources in Montana is licensed by the NRC, because Montana is not an Agreement State. Radiographers must meet NRC training and certification requirements under 10 CFR Part 34. X-ray equipment is regulated by the state. ASNT RT certification is a separate credential.

What does NDT training cost in Billings?

It depends on methods, levels, group size and delivery format. We quote each request, and cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Billings employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the usual basis for NDT personnel qualification at US refineries, pipelines and fabrication shops. Your employer's written practice and client specifications set the details.

Can a small Montana shop certify its own technicians?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. You need a written practice and access to a Level III, and that Level III can be an outside provider.

Does ASNT certification cover pipeline operator qualification?

No. Operator qualification for pipeline covered tasks is a separate requirement from NDT method certification.

Does Atlantis train for API or AWS inspector exams?

No. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A method training only. Candidates earn other credentials separately.

Can training be scheduled around winter and turnaround season?

Yes. Many Billings employers run theory in winter and practical exams just before the busy season.

What do NDT technicians earn in Montana?

It depends on level, methods and travel. Our NDT salary guide summarises published ranges.

How can I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Use our UT Level II practice questions and practise technique in the Practical NDT simulator.

Does cold weather affect ultrasonic testing in Montana?

Yes. Temperature changes sound velocity and couplant behaviour, so technicians should calibrate close to the part's temperature, use suitable couplants, and check calibration more often when conditions change.

Can penetrant testing be done outdoors in a Montana winter?

Only within the temperature range the procedure is qualified for. Below that range, the part has to be warmed or a procedure qualified for low temperature has to be used.
